subject: Trial success definitions, exit gates & sign-off checklist — Sentinel Health pilot
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@sentinelhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot trial — aligning on success criteria and signoffs

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for yesterday's demo — the team at Sentinel liked the throughput numbers and the latency profile you showed. We have a short internal window to run a 4-week pilot with a small production workload and we want to lock down: success criteria, exit gates (what causes stop/fail), and the exact acceptance tests we'll run so procurement can greenlight the trial.

High-level asks:
- A concise list of pass/fail acceptance tests (latency P95, throughput targets, token cost ceiling, quality/concordance thresholds for our clinical-extraction use case)
- A clear escalation/rollback plan if we hit regression or data issues
- Who signs the MAP and what are the exact signoff artifacts (e.g., acceptance CSV, SOC2 evidence checklist)

Can you send a draft MAP and an acceptance checklist that we can include in the procurement packet by next Monday (2026-03-08)?

Best,
Alex
Alex Ramos
Head of Integrations, Sentinel Health
alex.ramos@sentinelhealth.com
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sentinelhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot trial — aligning on success criteria and signoffs

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP and an acceptance-tests CSV that maps each test to owner, measurement method, pass threshold, and rollback trigger. Quick summary below.

Attachments: MAP_SentinelHealth_v0.9.pdf (draft MAP), sentinel-acceptance-tests.csv (detailed test matrix)

Summary (draft):
- Trial window: 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-12 (4 weeks).
- Acceptance tests (examples):
  1) Latency (API generation): P95 <= 450ms at 90% of observed traffic distribution (test harness: production-like replay).
  2) Throughput: sustain 120 requests/minute with 95% success (no service errors) during peak window.
  3) Quality: concordance on 500 labeled clinical-extracts >= 92% (F1) compared to ground truth.
  4) Cost: per-token unit cost ceiling <= $0.0009 (billing estimate) across run.
  5) Safety/PII: no storage of raw PHI in logs; KMS encryption enabled on all persisted artifacts (validated by SOC2 evidence checklist).

- Exit gates: any single critical regression in quality (>6 point absolute drop in F1 over a 24h sliding window) or repeated infra errors (>0.5% 5xx rate sustained for 1 hour) triggers an immediate pause and root-cause process.

- Signoff: Final sign-off (go/no-go) requires: acceptance-tests.csv signed by Sentinel QA lead, a confirmed SOC2 evidence snapshot for data handling controls, and Redwood's operational playbook (listed in MAP).

Next steps: Marcus and Stephanie will add the runbook-level checks and define marker artifacts for the procurement packet; Marcus, can you take the runbook/rollback bullets and add owner/SLR? Stephanie, please add the SOC2 evidence checklist we typically use for pilots.

Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Adding the operational checklist — I converted Kimberly's high-level exit gates into measurable runbook items and assigned owners. Key additions in the acceptance matrix (attached in the master sheet):

- Measurement methods:
  * Latency/Throughput: use our traffic-replay harness + sentinel-acceptance-tests.csv; collector runs every 15 minutes; alerts to on-call if P95 > threshold for two consecutive 15-min windows.
  * Quality validation: daily batch evaluation against the 500 labeled items; commit a summary artifact (daily_report_YYYYMMDD.csv) to the shared S3 bucket; Sentinel QA to verify sample artifacts on Monday/Thursday.
  * Cost monitoring: automated token accounting exported to the billing report every 24 hours; if projected monthly spend exceeds estimate by >12% we pause ingest and notify procurement.

- Rollback triggers and actions:
  1) Critical quality regression (>6 pt drop): immediate pause (API traffic moved to fallback model), incident declared, 4-hour hotfix/rollback window; post-mortem within 72 hours.
  2) Infra errors (5xx >0.5% sustained 1h): scale and failover; if not resolved in 30 minutes, pause trial and notify Sentinel execs.

- Owners: Marcus (runbook & monitoring), Stephanie (compliance evidence & SOC2 artifacts), Kimberly (stakeholder signoffs & procurement packet).

I've attached a one-page signoff checklist that procurement can include.

Marcus
Director, Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement needed. A few clarifying notes before we finalize: 

1) For the quality check, can we define the concordance metric as macro-averaged F1 across the 12 extraction fields we care about? We want a per-field breakdown attached to daily_report.
2) For the cost ceiling, Sentinel procurement asks that the trial estimate include worst-case projected tokens for a 30% traffic surge; please include that calc in the billing export.
3) On SOC2 evidence: we will want a signed attestation or a snapshot of the specific control docs (logging retention, KMS key ids) included in the procurement submission. If you can add that as a separate tab in the soc2 spreadsheet, great.

Assuming you can incorporate the two changes above, we can sign and return the acceptance-tests.csv and the MAP_v0.9 PDF by 2026-03-08 morning. Also please add the DocuSign envelope link for the MAP itself (procurement requires a signed MAP).

I'll loop in our QA lead once the per-field F1 outputs are attached.

– Priya Shah
Director, Procurement, Sentinel Health
